Amber Current Design Corp. submits this memorandum concerning disputed software acceptance testing. The present record does not support the sweeping relief sought by Mosaic Hill Labs Inc.. The chronology is especially important. On the morning in question, the project coordinator recorded that the reported failures arose from optional configurations outside the agreed test plan. Later correspondence repeated that account before litigation was anticipated. By contrast, the contrary declaration was prepared months later and does not identify its source of knowledge. The principal materials are the test scripts, defect ledger, and signed demonstration record. Those materials are authenticated by their respective custodians, reflect ordinary entries made at the time, and leave a factual question about responsibility. At this stage, reasonable inferences belong to the nonmoving party, and credibility disputes cannot be resolved from a paper record. Nor is a broader inquiry proportional here: the opposing request spans unrelated projects and years having no connection to the pleaded events. Accordingly, Amber Current Design Corp. asks the Court to enter judgment on the acceptance issue and reserve the calculation of any credit. That result preserves a fair determination on a complete record without granting either side an unwarranted procedural advantage.
